subject: Ordered Categorical Model with Known Covariance Matrix not Converging

messages.author: f42b0240615306ac
messages.subject: Ordered Categorical Model with Known Covariance Matrix not Converging
parts:
Dear Stan group,

My ordered categorical model is not converging, see the attached convergenceIssue.png. I have created the R code together with relevant R data for your convenience. Simply run convergenceIssue.R will catch the problem.

With my own diagnosis, the problem might come from the covariance matrix, KS, with most of its components 0. This matrix was created from another matrix, which is not positive-definite, by truncating all of its negative values to 0. Ironically, if I put the original non-positive-definite matrix into the model, the model converge well and faster. But I am afraid the results might be somehow problematic given that positive-definite matrix was required for the cholesky_decompose() function in the model.

Anyway, why the current KS matrix as attached not working? Are there illusive identificability or scale issues in the model?

Thanks much,

Xulong

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Ordered Categorical Model with Known Covariance Matrix not Converging
parts:
Positive definiteness isn't about the positiveness of the entries.
Check out the Wikipedia article for a definition and examples:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positive-definite_matrix

If the matrix isn't positive definite, the Cholesky decomposition
will fail with an error message in Stan.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Ordered Categorical Model with Known Covariance Matrix not Converging
parts:
Hi Bob, I understood positive definite isn't necessarily positiveness of the entries. I checked matrices positive definiteness with is.positive.definite function in a R package matrixcalc.

I truncated negative entries with 0 because 1, it make sense in terms of its meanings. This matrix defines genetic relatedness between individuals, negative coefficient and 0 can be viewed as equivalent. 2, it becomes positive-definite as reported with matrixcalc.

But since you mentioned Cholesky decomposition in Stan will thrown error message with non-positive-definite matrix. I will try different methods to check positive definiteness with the original matrix.

However, given that Cholesky decomposition in Stan did not fail with error message with the truncated matrix that I used. I believe the matrix itself is positive-definite for sure. But Stan did not converge with this matrix and I do not know what is going wrong.
